findings.finding: The FY order-intake target ('around the previous year's high level', about EUR 549m) is arithmetically out of reach after H1 order intake of EUR 263.0m (-9.4%) and against Q3 2025's EUR 141.1m comparison. The H1 report already dropped the numeric guide from its outlook wording, so the Q3 statement is the natural place to soften or formally abandon it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Order intake decided both of the last two quarterly prints despite earnings beats: Q1 on 2026-05-19, -12.3% (order intake EUR 131.1m vs 144.2m), and H1 on 2026-08-19, -11.96% (EUR 263.0m vs 290.2m, Q2 EPS 1.11 vs 0.86 estimate). FY2025 finals with the outlook, 2026-04-15: +9.98%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is down from 68.80 (H1 close) to about 60 and from 113 in May, and German commentary calls Q3 order intake decisive. A formal cut or removal of the order target has not been announced, and the April/May wording ('order intake anticipated to remain at the high level of the previous year') is still the last quantified statement. If the market had fully priced a guide cut, a 0.54% short would have been building and the stock would not have bounced 6% on Bernstein's initiation on 2026-10-23.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 comparison from the company's own Q3 2025 statement (https://www.pfisterer.com/sites/default/files/2025-11/PFISTERER%20Q3%20Financial%20statements%202025_fin_0.pdf: Q3 order intake 141,050 vs 122,250 kEUR). stock3 (de) on the H1 drop: 'Der Auftragseingang ist rückläufig, wichtige Regionen verlieren an Dynamik' (https://stock3.com/news/pfisterer-warum-der-highflyer-nach-starken-zahlen-einbricht-17249491).

findings.finding: Revenue and margin are tracking above the at-least-12% guide. H1 revenue was +20.2%, the backlog EUR 340.3m 'already extends into 2027', and the Q2 revenue run rate of EUR 129.8m against a Q3 2025 comparison of EUR 113.1m points to a Q3 near or slightly above the EUR 521.9m FY consensus path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue and EPS beats were sold twice in 2026 (Q1 -12.3%, H1 -11.96% with EPS 1.11 vs 0.86 estimate). Q3 2025 (revenue +25.5%): -3.9% on 2025-11-19, then +8.5% the next day.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced and inside guidance: the consensus of EUR 521.9m already assumes about +16%. The only unpriced part is the possibility of a revenue guide nudge (GBC quoted a management range of EUR 500-525m), which would show as revenue consensus migrating above 525. No such migration was found.

findings.finding: The company's H1 forecast was explicitly conditioned on the Middle East conflict easing ('based on the assumption that the ongoing conflict in the Middle East will ease in the short to medium term'), and it cited higher freight costs and longer delivery times. Tracker reports have Hormuz shipping still 'below normal' in November, so the assumption did not hold through Q3. The Middle East & India region was the source of the high prior-year orders behind the decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print isolated this line. H1 (2026-08-19, -11.96%) cited the decline of 'the high order volume from the Middle East & India region and the OHL product segment in prior periods'.
findings.why_not_priced: The conflict is public. What is not priced is whether the company now changes its forecast premise or quantifies the Gulf effect. Against that, it booked new Oman orders on 2026-11-04, which shows the region is still ordering. This is macro-to-company transmission, but the company itself named the dependency, so it is sized small rather than dropped.
findings.independence: Gulf News / UKMTO on Hormuz shipping 'below normal, but not stalled' (https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/hormuz-shipping-below-normal-but-not-stalled-1.500741839)

baseline_tension: The baseline lean is flat (+0.06) and the 20d run-up is +5.3% on a -16.2% 60d. My findings lean slightly negative on the guidance line, so they cut mildly against the 20d bounce and agree with the 60d de-rating that already reflects order fears. That is why p_up sits only 4 points below 50.
language_note: stock3 (de) explained the H1 sell-off as falling order intake, regions losing momentum, and the board making its optimistic statements concrete only on the analyst call. The English wire copy carried the order number but not this reading.

boerse-global (de) carried Oddo BHF's target cut from EUR 91 to 81 and the Bernstein initiation at EUR 102 with their timing around 2026-10-22/23. English searches surfaced Bernstein only without a date and did not surface the Oddo cut.
GBC via Deutsche Börse (de) gave management's 2026 revenue range of EUR 500-525m, which is absent from the company's English releases (they say 'at least 12%').
The primary documents (EQS releases, the H1 report, the presentations) are published in English, so German filings added nothing beyond them.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' (guidance findings 11 of 17, median 9.0% on a change): the order-intake guide finding is sized on the guidance scale, -1.5 to -2.0, with a wider range of -7 to +2.

'You were right about the number and too small about the move' and 'understatement is the systematic error': abs_move_pct raised from 8.0 to 9.0, closer to the name's own release-day moves of 10-12%. p_up stays near 50 rather than shrinking the size.

'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction' (this name sold both 2026 beats): the revenue-tracking finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, and p_up moved from 47 to 46 only because the guide line now carries more weight.
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series': the Nexans read-across cut from +0.5 to +0.4.
